informal_statement: Suppose that $h(x)=f^{-1}(x)$. If $h(2)=10$, $h(10)=1$ and $h(1)=2$, what is $f(f(10))$? Show that it is 1.
formal_statement:
theorem mathd_algebra_209
  (f h : ℝ → ℝ)
  (h₀: Function.LeftInverse f h)
  (h₁ : h 2 = 10)
  (h₂ : h 10 = 1)
  (h₃ : h 1 = 2) :
  f (f 10) = 1 := by sorry

informal_statement:
Determine all values $x$ in the interval $0\\leq x\\leq 2\\pi $
  which satisfy the inequality\n$2\\cos x \\leq \\left| \\sqrt{1+\\sin 2x} - \\sqrt{1-\\sin 2x } \\right| \\leq \\sqrt{2}.$
  Prove that x must be
  1. \\pi / 4 ≤ x
  2. x ≤ 7 * \\pi / 4
formal_statement:
theorem imo_1965_p1 (x : ℝ) (h₀ : 0 ≤ x) (h₁ : x ≤ 2 * Real.pi)
  (h₂ : 2 * Real.cos x ≤ abs (Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sin (2 * x)) - Real.sqrt (1 - Real.sin (2 * x))))
  (h₃ : abs (Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sin (2 * x)) - Real.sqrt (1 - Real.sin (2 * x))) ≤ Real.sqrt 2) :
  Real.pi / 4 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 7 * Real.pi / 4 := by sorry
